entry.title: UIFramework v1.8.1: UIFramework v1.8.1 (pre-release)
entry.content:
The first part of a review of the whole framework: the mistakes a streamer can run into. Games need no update for the window's fixes; the two in the host block reach a game with its next release.

Fixed

  • AltGr no longer counts as Ctrl. AltGr is Ctrl+Alt to Windows, so on a German keyboard { (AltGr+7) jumped to the seventh page of a window instead of being typed, [, ] and } likewise in windows with eight to ten pages; on a Spanish one @ and # went to page two and three. The window's shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+1 to 0) now take Ctrl without Alt.
  • Typing is left alone by an action that follows the fields. A window with an auto + live action (Trivia's difficulty line) looked at the fields 350 ms after every change, and that look ended the edit of a table cell and turned a half-typed name into a chip (alice,bob became alice, bo, b). It now reads what is there and touches nothing.
  • turnTimeout has no minimum of its own. The conventions' min: 5 went to every game that declared none, so Blackjack's "0 = no limit" was shown as 0 and saved as 5. A game that wants a floor declares it (Battleship does).
  • One game's failed release check no longer silences the update notice. A repository without a published release, a renamed one or GitHub's rate limit kept the notice waiting for good, for every game and for UIFramework itself. Such a game is now left out of that run's notice; only UIFramework's own check (no network) still holds it.
  • A list whose file could not be read cannot be edited. It was not written, as the red i said, but rows could be typed into it and Save answered "Saved". It is greyed out now, with the reason as its tooltip (list.unreadable, in English, German and Spanish).
  • Tip("search") is no mistake. The stop was shown, but the declaration check did not know the part and put a problem behind the red i.
  • The Log page lets go of its folder when the window closes. Its watcher was stopped only when the page was rebuilt; every window closed left one behind, holding the whole closed window, until Streamer.bot ended.
  • A game's own page title comes first. Pg("board", "Rangliste") lost to the conventions' translation of the wording "Board" (the grid, "Spielfeld"), so Hangman's scoreboard page was titled "Spielfeld" in German.
  • The tour leaves Alt+F4 and Alt+Space to the window.
  • Host block: UiTimer.Rearm leaves a timer off that was switched off between its tick and the game's run; before, that run switched the automatic start back on.
  • Host block: the DLL is loaded the way the settings action loads it. For the update notice and UiLive the block used LoadFrom, which refuses a DLL saved from a browser, did not know a folder named v1.8.0, and did not look at the .sha256 beside the DLL. It now uses UnsafeLoadFrom, takes the v, and leaves a DLL alone that no longer matches its hash.
  • Demo game: the Execute Code sub-actions of DemoGame.sb carry their actions' names, so an Execute C# Method sub-action elsewhere can pick them.

Changed

  • docs/Loader.md and docs/Getting-Started.md no longer say that a game action never loads the DLL: it does, for the update notice and the live check, which is also why a framework update is usually used from the next start of Streamer.bot.

entry.title: Trivia Game v9.3.0: An Addicted cut you set, rounds at random times, StartRound (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • The Addicted cut is a setting. Viewers on the addicted list always lost half of every win. Addicted cut under Addicted on the Access page now says how much: 50 as before, 20 for a lighter touch, 0 for none. The message for a viewer added to the list names it as {addictedCut}; one saved with "50%" written out follows the setting too.
  • Rounds while Twitch runs ads. Under Ad breaks on the new Automation page: Start a round when ads start plays as many rounds as fit the ad break, Announce it before the ads says so in chat 1 to 5 minutes ahead, Bonus during ads makes rounds started during a break pay more, and Rounds only during ads keeps viewers' starts to the breaks. Twitch only; the import brings the Ad Run and Upcoming Ad triggers for it, and Trivia: Ad Break Started and Trivia: Ad Break Ended are there for your own actions.
  • An Automation page. The rounds that start themselves moved there from the Game page, next to the ad breaks.
  • Rounds at random times, and only once chat has been talking. Under Rounds that start themselves on the Automation page, Random time draws every wait anew between Every and At most, and Only after chat lines holds a round back until a platform's chat has written that many lines since its last automatic round. Together with the fixed interval these are the three ways a Streamer.bot timer can run.
  • StartRound for your own actions. An Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action starts a round from any action: a hotkey, a Stream Deck button, a raid. Optional arguments triviaPlatform, triviaRounds and triviaCategory; it sets triviaStarted and triviaStartedOn. No cooldown and no moderator check apply.
  • Triggers and methods on the Help page. The page now ends with every custom trigger and its arguments, and the methods for your own actions. Fire with sample values under a trigger fires it once, so an action of yours that listens to it can be tried without playing. Needs UIFramework 1.6.0, which the settings fetch by themselves.

Changed

  • The live check is UIFramework's. Asking Twitch and Kick whether you are live moved into UIFramework 1.6.0, where Hangman uses it too. Until the settings have been opened once with that version, recent chat decides in its place, and Streamer.bot's log says so once.

entry.title: Hangman Game v13.3.0: Rounds that start themselves, and StartRound (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • A round while Twitch runs ads. Under Ad breaks on the new Automation page: Start a round when ads start starts one with the ad break, as a blitz round if you like; Announce it before the ads says so in chat 1 to 5 minutes ahead; Bonus during ads makes a round started during a break pay more; Rounds only during ads keeps viewers' starts to the breaks. Twitch only; the import brings the Ad Run and Upcoming Ad triggers for it, and Hangman: Ad Break Started and Hangman: Ad Break Ended are there for your own actions.
  • Rounds that start themselves. A new section on the Automation page switches on the timed action [HM] - Auto Hangman Timer, which starts a round on every platform you are live on where none is running. It runs the three ways a Streamer.bot timer can: Every so many minutes, at a Random time drawn anew between Every and At most, and Only after chat lines, which holds a round back until a platform's chat has written that many lines since its last automatic round (10 by default). No moderator and no cooldown is needed for these rounds.
  • StartRound for your own actions. An Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action starts a round from any action: a hotkey, a Stream Deck button, a raid. Optional arguments hangmanPlatform and hangmanBlitz; it sets hangmanStarted and hangmanStartedOn. No cooldown and no moderator check apply.
  • Automatic rounds only where you are live. Twitch is asked through its API, YouTube by the broadcasts Streamer.bot monitors, Kick through its channel page (UIFramework 1.6.0). A platform that cannot say goes by whether its chat has written anything since the last automatic round.
  • Triggers and methods on the Help page. The page now ends with every custom trigger and its arguments, and the methods for your own actions. Fire with sample values under a trigger fires it once, so an action of yours that listens to it can be tried without playing. Needs UIFramework 1.6.0, which the settings fetch by themselves.

Changed

  • The import carries a timed action, three chat triggers and two ad triggers. Twitch, YouTube and Kick chat messages now reach the game action, which only counts them for Only after chat lines. Import the new file once when updating, so the timed action and the triggers exist; pasting the code alone leaves automatic rounds without their timer.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.8.0: UIFramework v1.8.0 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • Search with Ctrl+F. Ctrl+F, or the new magnifier at the top right, opens a search bar in every window. It finds settings (by label, help, section, page and key), messages and pages; every word typed has to occur, in any order, whatever the case and the accents. Up and Down move, Enter goes there: the page comes to the front and the field is scrolled into view, ringed for a moment and given the cursor. Games declare nothing for it and need no update; Tip("search") adds the magnifier to a window's tour. See The search in docs/Schema.md.
  • UIFramework.Preview -windowshots <folder> -search <text> photographs the search bar with that typed in, and where its first result leads.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.7.0: UIFramework v1.7.0 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • UiAdBreak: Twitch's ad break as a window of time for a game. Chat stays usable while ads run, so that is when a round fits. Begin opens the window from Streamer.bot's Ad Run trigger for the ads' length (there is no trigger for their end), Active and SecondsLeft say whether ads run, Announce answers the Upcoming Ad trigger once per break, RoundsThatFit and WithBonus do the sums. See Twitch's ad breaks in docs/Schema.md.
  • An Automation page in the conventions, with five keys for the ad break (adBreakStart, adBreakAnnounce, adBreakAnnounceMinutes, adBreakBonusPercent, adBreakOnly) in English, German and Spanish.

Changed

  • The timer's keys (autoStart…) are on the Automation page instead of Game. A game that names their page itself is not affected.
  • Trivia and Hangman start rounds with ad breaks and have the Automation page.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.6.0: UIFramework v1.6.0 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • Custom triggers and methods are declared once. UiWindow.Trigger, Triggers (several that share their arguments) and Method say what a game offers the streamer's own actions. UiTriggers.Register in Init() registers the triggers from that list, and the Help page ends with Custom triggers and Methods for your own actions, each with its arguments, in English, German and Spanish.
  • Fire with sample values. A button under each trigger on the Help page has the game fire it once with its sample values, so an action that listens to it can be tried without playing a round.
  • UiLive: whether you are live. Twitch through its API with Streamer.bot's token, YouTube by the monitored broadcasts, Kick through its channel page; Live, Offline or Unknown, never an exception. Twitch and Kick are asked by the DLL, since the host block must compile in an action without System.dll. Trivia's own check moved here, and Hangman's automatic rounds use it.
  • tools\copy-host-block.ps1, and -Into / -HostName on update-host-block.ps1: the block a game carries goes into its other action and into hosts\<host>\HostBlock.cs in one step, with -Check to compare.

Changed

  • A conventions key hands on its requires, so the timer's intervals are greyed out with their switch in a game that declares them with key and default alone (already in 1.5.0, not listed there).
  • Trivia, Hangman, Blackjack and Battleship declare their triggers and methods this way.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.5.0: UIFramework v1.5.0 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • A timed action on a random time and after chat lines. Streamer.bot's timer dialog offers a fixed interval, a random one and "only after so many chat lines", but code can set only the interval. UiTimer in the host block keeps the other two: Sync brings the timed action in line with the settings (a running timer keeps its countdown unless the schedule was just saved), Rearm draws a random timer's next wait each time it fires, and NoteLine / TakeLines count chat lines per platform and hold a start back until there are enough. See A timed action in docs/Schema.md.
  • Five convention keys for it: autoStartEnabled, autoStartIntervalMinutes, autoStartRandom, autoStartIntervalMaxMinutes and autoStartMinChatLines, with page, row, labels and help in English, German and Spanish. A game declares them with key and default alone.

Changed

  • Trivia and Hangman run their automatic rounds on it (Trivia v9.3.0, Hangman v13.3.0). The host copies of Trivia, Hangman, Blackjack and Battleship are the games' current ones.

entry.title: Trivia Game v9.2.2: Every time field says its unit
entry.content:
The settings window now names the unit of every time field, so it is clear that the delay between rounds is in seconds.

Fixed

  • Every time field says its unit. Answer time, first reminder, delay between rounds, the blitz times, both cooldowns and the overlay's result time carried no unit in the settings window, while the automatic-round fields said "(minutes)". They now read "(s)", and those two "(min)".

Your settings stay as they are: the values were always seconds and minutes, only the labels changed.

entry.title: Trivia Game v9.2.1: The overlay follows chat
entry.content:
The OBS overlay mirrors what chat is asked again: automatic rounds only go to the platforms you are live on, a chip names the platform a question went to, a &demo=1 left in the source's URL no longer stands in for the game, and the result of a round is shown for its full time before the next question of a run.

Added

  • The overlay names the platform. A chip in front of the question says whether it went to Twitch, YouTube or Kick, for streaming to more than one at once, where every platform plays a question of its own. Which platform it came from under What it shows on the Overlay page turns it off.

Fixed

  • The overlay follows chat even with &demo=1 in its URL. The Try the demo answer told you to add &demo=1 to the OBS source to place it, and an overlay with it never listened to Streamer.bot: it played its three sample questions on their own 10 to 12 second clocks for every stream after, whatever chat was asked. A demo now listens too, and the first real round ends the samples for good. The answer now points to Show a sample round.
  • The overlay's result is shown for its full time in a run. The next question waited for Delay between rounds alone, 5 seconds by default, and cut a 10 second result short. While the overlay is on, it now waits until the result, and the leaderboard after it when that is on, has been up for Result shown for.
  • Automatic rounds only go where you are live. A round was offered to every platform with a connected account, or with Only when chat has been active off to Twitch, YouTube and Kick alike: chats you were not streaming to got questions, and the overlay showed whichever platform's question started last over the one your chat was asked. The timed action now asks each platform first: Twitch through its API with Streamer.bot's own login, YouTube through the broadcasts Streamer.bot monitors, Kick through its public channel page. Where it cannot be told, recent chat decides, as before.
  • The check before saving only asks about what you changed. It named every problem the settings had on every save, so Save & Exit right after a save asked again about something you had already kept on purpose, such as Only when chat has been active switched off. It now asks only about the problems the save brings in.

After importing, save the settings once with the overlay on, so the new overlay page is written to Chat Games\Trivia Game\Overlay. If your OBS source's URL still carries &demo=1, click Set it up in OBS to point it at the plain URL again. Rounds that start themselves now wait until you are live: nothing starts while you are offline.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.4.3: UIFramework v1.4.3 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Fixed

  • A table's columns end at its edge. A list shown as a table (Trivia's own questions) left an empty column after its last one: the columns were sized as if the vertical scrollbar always showed, and the whole pixels lost a few more. They now share the width the rows really have, with the scrollbar only while it shows, and follow it as rows are added or removed; what is left over goes to the widest column.

entry.title: Slot Machine Game v16.4.0: Tells you about updates
entry.content:
Once per Streamer.bot start, about 20 seconds in, one notice names new releases of this game, of the other UIFramework games and of UIFramework: in every chat whose broadcaster account is connected (Twitch, YouTube, Kick), or as a Windows notification while none is. Tell me about updates on the About page turns it off. On UIFramework for streamer.bot 1.4.0.

Added

  • Tells you about updates. Once per Streamer.bot start, about 20 seconds in, one notice names new releases of this game, of the other UIFramework games and of UIFramework: in every chat whose broadcaster account is connected (Twitch, YouTube, Kick), or as a Windows notification while none is. The links are in Streamer.bot's log. Tell me about updates on the About page turns it off for this game. The game action is precompiled on application start, so the notice starts with Streamer.bot.
  • The host block is UIFramework 1.4.0's; the settings window offers the newest UIFramework on its next open.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.4.1: UIFramework v1.4.1 (pre-release)
entry.content:

entry.title: Battleship Game v2.2.0: A tour of the window, an overlay demo and Free game from chat
entry.content:
The overlay can play a made-up battle to place and style it, moderators switch Free game from chat, and every finished battle fires a trigger your own actions can use. On UIFramework for streamer.bot 1.0.0, the settings window shows you around on its first open, and problems it finds sit behind one red i in its header.

Added

  • A tour of the settings window. The first time the window opens, a short tour rings one part after the other (the pages, saving, the customise mode) and says what it does; the ? at the top right shows it again.
  • UIFramework 1.0.0. Problems the window finds sit behind a red i in its header instead of on the About or Log page, and How to play, Log and About sit together at the foot of the page list. The settings action offers the new framework on its next open.

📺 Overlay

  • Try the demo. A new button on the Overlay page opens the overlay in your browser, playing a short made-up battle in the saved look (a miss, a sunk destroyer, the Admiral finding your cruiser, the enemy fleet sunk), without Streamer.bot. With ?demo=1 on the overlay's address, OBS plays it the same way, to place and size the source.
  • Show a sample round. The button beside it plays that battle once on every overlay that is open, the one in OBS included, so you can check where it sits and how it looks; then the overlay goes back to no battle. Not while a real battle runs. The overlay is version 17 and replaces an older copy on the next command, keeping that one as a .bak; an overlay already open in OBS reloads itself within ten seconds.

🆓 Free game from chat

  • Two moderator commands. !SetFreeBattleship turns Free game on and !EndFreeBattleship turns it off (they come with the import, disabled and set to the Moderators group). The switch is written into the settings file, so the window's pill shows it, and chat gets the new Started and Ended messages (Messages page, Free game). An action of your own can do the same with an Execute C# Method on StartFreeGame or EndFreeGame of the game action.
  • Two more custom triggers. BSG: Free Game Start and BSG: Free Game End fire whenever Free game is switched that way.

🪟 Settings window

  • The settings action is UIFramework's stub 0.2.0. When the game action hangs, the settings window waits 30 seconds for its answer, then carries on and can be closed; before, it waited for good. A game that has not described itself for a minute no longer locks the settings until Streamer.bot restarts: the next run opens the window.

  • The host block is UIFramework's current one (1.0.0). It names every type in full, so it no longer depends on the action's using lines, and it can declare a tour of the window. Nothing changes in the window.

  • German. With the window's language set to de (the pencil, then Sprache), every setting, section, page and message of the window reads in German. The help and about pages, the summaries and the presets' status line stay English.

  • The settings action is UIFramework's generic stub. [BG] - .Settings carries no layout and no code of its own any more: the game action declares its window (pages, the log, help and about, the cooldowns of !battleship) beside its settings table and answers the window itself. Reset the leaderboard now, Set the overlay up in OBS and Add to OBS now answer with what happened instead of "queued", and a save puts the Click to Fire settings on a live overlay as before. Needs UIFramework 0.9.2 or newer; the stub fetches it.

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers. Every finished battle fires a trigger (Custom > Chat Game > Battleship Game): BSG: Battle Won, BSG: Battle Lost, BSG: Battle Timed Out or BSG: Battle Stopped for a solo battle, BSG: Chat Battle Settled for the chat's battle, BSG: Duel Settled for a team duel, and BSG: Battle Settled for every one of them. The trigger carries the battle as arguments: battleOutcome (the log's result: WIN, LOSS, TIMEOUT, NO-SHOW, STOPPED), battleMode (solo, chat or duel), battleUser, battleUserId, battlePlatform, battleTrigger (fire, timeout or stop), battleBoard, battleShots, battleHits, battleAccuracy, battleShipsSunk, battleShipsLost, battleNet (the battle's total, or a duel's pot), battleWinner (a duel's winning side) and battleCurrency. GetLastBattleResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands the same arguments to any other action.
